clue.text: To express in other words might appear rash

indicators.note: the letters show what they might become when rearranged, hinting they can be reshuffled into a new word

explanation.surface: Restating something could look hasty or reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might appear' reads as a hedge, but 'might' is the signal to rearrange APPEARRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate a passage in your own wording is the standard meaning.

clue.text: Prepare to leave the crowd

definitions.meaning: to put belongings in a case before a trip
a gang or herd of people or animals

explanation.definitionFit: One verb sense is filling luggage before departure; one noun sense is a group moving together, a herd or mob.

clue.text: It was reconstructed by butler, I revealed

indicators.note: the letters of the words are laid out anew so that a fresh word is revealed from them

explanation.surface: A servant confesses that he was the one who put something back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' signals rearranging BUTLERI; 'It was' and 'by' are surface padding around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put together again after being destroyed has been made anew, a synonym.

clue.text: Many support Leonard in the old tough synthetic material

parts.note: poly- is the prefix meaning many
a prop is a support

indicators.note: the name sits inside the archaic word, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
Len is short for Leonard

explanation.surface: A list of plastics ingredients reads like a crowd backing a man called Leonard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic polymer of propylene, widely used for rope, packaging and fibres, an example of a hard-wearing synthetic.

clue.text: Brought back to health although laid up again!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
goods laid up are stored away

explanation.surface: Someone recovered even though they had been bedridden once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' suggests being ill in bed, fitting the health picture, but here it means put away in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient made well again has had their health returned to them, a synonym.

clue.text: Present day stocking filler

parts.note: reads as a modern small gift, but means the figure who fills stockings with presents on Christmas Day

explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas fills children's stockings with gifts on the day itself.

clue.text: Dog in a narrow escape kennelled

indicators.note: the dog is said to be in the following words, whose letters contain it

explanation.surface: A dog had a close call before being shut in its kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog runs across 'escaPE KEnnelled'; 'a narrow' adds to the picture of a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Pekingese, a small long-haired Chinese breed of toy hound.

clue.text: I am the most important to him

definitions.text: I am the most important to him

parts.words: I am the most important to him
parts.note: a person whose own self matters above all else, so the word I is supreme in his thinking

explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person who thinks only of himself and talks constantly about himself.

clue.text: Not a bit of it

parts.note: sounds like a flat denial, but read literally means the whole thing rather than a small part

explanation.definitionFit: The entire lot rather than any single portion of it.

clue.text: Accountant and graduate left small party

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: An accountant and a graduate walked out of a modest gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration; here it is a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret political clique or faction, a small group plotting together.

clue.text: Suitable material for building a castle at the seaside?

definitions.text: Suitable material for building a castle at the seaside?

parts.words: Suitable material for building a castle at the seaside?
parts.note: a sandcastle on the beach would need beach grains, and this is a real building rock made of them

explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary rock of compressed grains, used for building, the beach grains in solid form.

clue.text: Use the same adhesive to support each other!

definitions.meaning: literally to glue things with one shared glue

explanation.surface: Glue advice doubles as a call for solidarity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to bond physically with glue and to remain loyal friends through difficulty.

clue.text: It is unlikely to come off

definitions.text: It is unlikely to come off

parts.words: It is unlikely to come off
parts.note: a thing not expected to succeed or happen, described as a quality of unlikeliness

explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being not expected to happen, i.e. something with little chance of success.

clue.text: Grime, a non-U mess, that's charming

indicators.note: the letters are made into a mess, jumbled up into another order

explanation.surface: Dirt and an unrefined mess are oddly delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' signals rearranging GRIMEANONU. Non-U is British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming someone means captivating them, filling them with love, a synonym.

clue.text: Gas, neon mixed with grit particles

indicators.note: the two words are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A gas formed when neon is combined with bits of grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neon' looks like the gas, but it is anagram fodder with GRIT, signalled by 'mixed'; 'particles' just decorates.
explanation.definitionFit: An element that makes up most of the air, an example of a gas.

clue.text: Picture boat heading south

indicators.note: the compass letter is placed at the head, in front of the vessel

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A painting of a vessel sailing southward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading south' reads as a direction of travel; 'heading' instead puts S at the front of KETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing, a type of picture.

clue.text: Became aware of codings 'e revised

indicators.note: the letters are revised, reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that he reworked some programming codes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' signals rearranging CODINGSE; 'e is dialect for he.
explanation.definitionFit: Became cognisant of, knew or perceived, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Melanie included your old chemical

indicators.note: the old pronoun is included within the short name, placed inside it

parts.note: Mel is short for Melanie
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A woman named Melanie adds an old possession of yours to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical of one carbon and three hydrogens, a chemical group in methanol.

clue.text: Chirpy speaker?

parts.note: reads as a cheerful talker, but a bird that chirps or a loudspeaker for high-pitched sounds

explanation.definitionFit: A loudspeaker reproducing high frequencies, also a chirping bird or social-media poster.

clue.text: Vehicle to go bang crashing

indicators.note: the words are crashing together, so their letters are broken and reordered

explanation.surface: A vehicle exploding in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow sled for sliding down snowy slopes, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: A stooge managed to become a sailor

indicators.note: the letters are managed, organised into another order

explanation.surface: A sidekick succeeded in joining the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' looks like 'succeeded'; it signals rearranging ASTOOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up a seafaring life is the idiom for joining a ship's crew.

clue.text: Not a flat race apparently between unequal rivals

definitions.meaning: humorously a horse race over bumpy ground, uneven rather than flat

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is a race over bumpy ground; idiomatically it is a mismatch between a strong and weak opponent.

clue.text: One hundred about to perform part of the service

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
re means about or concerning
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A hundred people are set to act in a church ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The creed, a statement of belief recited in the church liturgy, part of the Mass.

clue.text: Settled by one in one's own house

indicators.note: the numeral goes in the home, placed inside it

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone settled in at home on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been settled has been paid off, a synonym.

clue.text: She went in order to be topical

indicators.note: the words are put in a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: She entered so that she would be current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' reads as purpose; 'order' signals rearranging SHEWENTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reported in current media coverage means being of current interest.

clue.text: Innkeeper has a flowering plant

parts.note: a host is one who receives guests, like an innkeeper

explanation.surface: A publican owns a blooming plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade-loving perennial with broad leaves and lily-like flowers, an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Banking system used by Inland Revenue Office after the end of the morning

indicators.note: the office comes after the letter, placed behind it
the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: IRO, abbreviation for Inland Revenue Office

explanation.surface: A payment system used by the tax office from late morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was Britain's former tax authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of credit transfer between bank or post-office accounts, a banking method.

clue.text: Where Alice might have speculated

parts.note: Lewis Carroll's heroine went to a fantasy realm, which split in two would be a place for pondering

explanation.definitionFit: The fantasy realm visited by Alice in Lewis Carroll's book, also a place to ponder.
